intended_object: The degree over K of the finite part of the different divisor of a finite separable extension L/K(X). That is, Σ_q d_q · deg_K(q) taken over the places q of L above the finite places p of K(X), where d_q is the exponent of q in the different and deg_K(q) = f(q|p)·deg(p). Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the degree formula proved later in the same file.
explanation:
How the body is built:
- `differentMultiplicityDivisor K[X] O_L` is the finitely supported function sending q to `multiplicity q.asIdeal (differentIdeal K[X] O_L)`, i.e. the different exponent d_q, at each height-one prime q of the integral closure of K[X] in L.
- For each q, the summand is d_q · `inertiaDeg` · `ratFuncFinitePlaceDegree`. Mathlib's `inertiaDeg` is [κ(q) : κ(p)] with p = q ∩ K[X]. `ratFuncFinitePlaceDegree` is the degree of the monic generator of p, which equals [κ(p) : K].
- So each summand is d_q · [κ(q) : K], and the sum is the usual degree over K of the finite different divisor.

This matches how the library uses it. In `finiteExtensionCanonicalDifferentDivisor_degree`, it is the finite contribution to the degree of the divisor of dX. Its weights agree with `finiteExtensionPlaceDegree` on finite places, as the proof of `hfinite` shows.

The result lands in ℕ, which is harmless because different exponents are non-negative. The hypothesis that the different is nonzero always holds in the separable setting (`finiteExtensionFiniteDifferentIdeal_ne_bot`).

The setting L/K(X) is not an artificial restriction. The notion of "finite places" relative to K[X], and the base place degree, only make sense once a rational base field has been fixed.

Mathlib has the different ideal and the inertia degree, but no degree of a different divisor for function fields. So there is no broader counterpart.
